Rashi on Pesachim 102a:1:1.hebrew: מאן תנא - להך ברייתא דקתני אע"ג דדברים הטעונין ברכה לאחריהן צריך לברך, רבי יהודה היא:
Rashi on Pesachim 102a:1:1.english: Who is the Tanna - [Of] this baraita that teaches that even though [they are] items that require a blessing after them, one must recite a blessing [anew] — it is Rabbi Yehuda.

Rashi on Pesachim 102a:2:1.english: Friends who were reclining and uprooted [themselves], etc. - And we do not have the reading "to drink wine."

Rashi on Pesachim 102a:3:1.hebrew: ומקשינן: אלא טעמא דבדברים הטעונין ברכה לאחריהם - משום הכי פליגי רבנן עליה דר' יהודה:
Rashi on Pesachim 102a:3:1.english: And we ask: Rather, the reason is that [it is] with items that require a blessing after them - Because of this, the Rabbis disagree with Rabbi Yehuda.

Rashi on Pesachim 102a:3:2.english: Thus, regarding items that do not require a blessing after them - Even the Rabbis concede that one must recite a blessing another time at the beginning.

Rashi on Pesachim 102a:4:1.hebrew: לימא תיהוי תיובתא דרבי יוחנן - דאמר לעיל, שינוי מקום אין צריך לברך, ולא מפליג בין דברים הטעונין לדברים שאינן טעונין:
Rashi on Pesachim 102a:4:1.english: Shall we say that this is a refutation of Rabbi Yochanan - Who said above [that for] a change of place one does not need to recite a blessing, and he does not distinguish between things that require [a blessing] and things that do not.

Rashi on Pesachim 102a:4:2.english: Didn't we refute him once - Above.

Rashi on Pesachim 102a:7:1.hebrew: ה"ג תניא כוותיה דרב חסדא חברים שהיו מסובין לשתות יין כו' - והיינו כרב חסדא דאמר דברים שטעונין ברכה לאחריהן, אין צריך לברך; והא בהדיא מסייעא לרב חסדא מדקתני יין, אבל בההיא דלעיל לא תנא יין בהדי':
Rashi on Pesachim 102a:7:1.english: Thus we read: "It was taught in accordance with Rav Chisda: Friends who were reclining to drink wine, etc." - And this is in accordance with Rav Chisda, who said [that for] things that require a blessing after them [in their place], one does not need to recite a [new] blessing [upon returning]. And this [baraita] explicitly supports Rav Chisda, since it teaches "wine," whereas in that [baraita] above, it did not teach "wine" explicitly.

Rashi on Pesachim 102a:8:1.english: And he recites over it the sanctification of the day - In the middle of his meal.

Rashi on Pesachim 102a:8:2.hebrew: ושני - מיד אומר עליו ברהמ"ז ומפסיק, כדאמר ר' יהודה לעיל, ומיהו הואיל והגיע עונת קידוש צריך לקדש תחלה. לא גרסינן: ראשון אומר עליו ברכת המזון, שני אומר עליו קדושת היום:
Rashi on Pesachim 102a:8:2.english: And a second [cup] - Immediately he recites Grace after Meals over it and interrupts [his meal], as Rabbi Yehuda said above; however, since the time for kiddush has arrived, he must recite kiddush first. We do not read [the text as]: "[Over] the first he recites Grace after Meals, [and over] the second he recites the sanctification of the day."

Tosafot on Pesachim 102a:2:1.hebrew: ועקרו רגליהם לילך לבהכ"נ כו' - מכאן משמע שאם שכח להתפלל ונזכר באמצע סעוד', והתפלל — שא"צ ברכה אפי' לכתחל'. ומה שהביא ה"ר יום טוב ראיה מפרק כיסוי הדם (חולין ד' פז.), דאמר: "מישתא וברוכי בהדי הדדי לא אפשר", שצריך לברך ברהמ"ז וליטול ידיו — אינה ראיה; דדוקא גבי ברהמ"ז אמרינן הכי, דהוי הפסק וגמר סעודה, אבל תפלה, אע"ג דמיכל וצלוי בהדי הדדי לא אפשר — אין בכך כלום:
Tosafot on Pesachim 102a:2:1.english: "And they uprooted themselves to go to the synagogue, etc." - From here it is implied that if one forgot to pray and remembered in the middle of a meal and prayed, he does not require a blessing even at the outset. And that which Rabbi Yom Tov brought a proof from the chapter [entitled] Kisui HaDam (Chullin 87a), where it says: "Drinking and reciting a blessing together is not possible," [meaning] that one must recite Grace After Meals and wash his hands — [this] is not a proof; for specifically regarding Grace After Meals do we say this, since it is an interruption and the conclusion of the meal, but [regarding] prayer, even though eating and praying together is not possible, it is of no consequence:

Tosafot on Pesachim 102a:7:1.hebrew: תניא כוותיה דרב חסדא - פי' רשב"ם: הא דלא מייתי כרב חסדא מרבנן דר' יהודה, משום דבההיא לא קתני בהדיא "יין". וזה פי' לפי שיטתו דגרסי' הכא "יין". וי"ל: משום הכי לא מייתי סייעתא מינה, משום דאיכא דאמרי בסנהדרין (ד' כה.) ד"במה" נמי לפרש. ואע"ג דחזרו, מייתי ראיה לרב חסדא, דטעמא דשינוי מקום דצריך לברך — משום שעמידתו ממקומו היא גמר אכילתו, וה"ה נמי חזרו:
Tosafot on Pesachim 102a:7:1.english: It was taught in accordance with Rav Ḥisda - Rashbam explained: The reason [the Gemara] does not bring [a proof] for Rav Ḥisda from the Rabbis who [disagree with] Rabbi Yehuda is because in that [baraita] "wine" is not explicitly taught. And he explained this according to his approach, that we read "wine" here [in our baraita]. And one can say: For this reason [the Gemara] does not bring support from it, because there are those who say in Sanhedrin (25a) that [the term] "bameh" ["in what case"] is also [used] to explain [rather than to disagree]. And even though [our baraita states] that they returned, [the Gemara] brings a proof for Rav Ḥisda, because the reason that a change of location requires one to recite a blessing is that his standing up from his place is the completion of his eating, and the same applies even [when] they returned.
